newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says Deng's condition "serious" - reports.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says Deng's condition "serious" - reports.

text.p: Taiwan's top policy-maker on mainland affairs has described the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping as "serious" and said the government would closely watch developments, local reports said on Tuesday.
The mass circulation United Daily News quoted Chang King-yuh, chairman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, as saying Taiwan has a full knowledge regarding Deng's health.
"According to sources from relevant authorities, (Deng's) condition this time is indeed very serious," the United Daily News quoted Chang as saying. He did not elaborate.
The council formulates Taiwan's policies towards China, which has been the island's bitter rival since the Chinese civil war split them in 1949.
The ruling Nationalist Party's Central Daily News also quoted Chang as saying reports of Deng's deteriorating health "seems real" and Taiwan would watch the developments closely.
Asked how Taiwan would react to Deng's death, Chang told the United Daily News that the Mainland Affairs Council and other government agencies would be ready when it happened.
He said it was inappropriate for the council to comment further before Beijing's official statement.
Chang could not be reached for comment.
Sources in Beijing on Monday said Deng's deteriorating health had forced Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to return to Beijing.

Deng, 92, whose pragmatic policies transformed a backward Stalinist state into an economic powerhouse, lives in a tightly guarded compound behind the Forbidden City of China's emperors in central Beijing.

Diplomats have said one barometer of Deng's health in China's highly secretive system was the movements of top leaders and close family members, with few willing to be out of town or abroad if Deng were close to death.
Chinese sources have reported increasing rumours in Beijing in the past few days that Deng's health might be failing.

Deng has not been seen in public since the 1994 Chinese Lunar New Year festival when he visited Shanghai and appeared frail and faltering. He is now believed to be in fragile health and with fading lucidity.
